# Implementation Plan: Suppress lead `<|report kind=...|>` footer-tag requirement (crews v1.7.4)

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-05-28. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan .ralph/jobs/crews-lead-suppress-kind-tag/plan.md`.*

## Overview

The crews plugin's SessionStart briefing and Stop hook both require every actor to end every turn with a `<|report kind="..." summary="..."|>` footer tag. The footer is essential for **members** because the lead's mailbox parser routes envelopes by `kind`. For **leads**, no consumer reads the footer — the lead has no orchestrator above it. The footer is therefore visual noise the operator finds unhelpful.

This change makes the requirement role-asymmetric: members keep emitting and Stop keeps enforcing; leads emit prose only, Stop accepts a missing tag, and the manifest's `lastSummary` is derived from the first line of the lead's prose (the existing `synthesizeSummary(body)` fallback). Internally the lead's `lastKind` defaults to `'progress'` so the existing outbox-append + manifest-update path stays intact without schema changes.

Ships as crews **v1.7.4** (patch — defensive UX improvement, no API change, no manifest schema change).

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context (`D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/`)
- `hooks/briefing/template.js` lines 68-219 already composes the briefing from named sections, each with a `lines: ctx => [...]` function. The existing `listener-arm` section (template.js:13-65) demonstrates the role-aware early-return pattern. The `footer-tag` section (template.js:108-130) is the primary instruction block to gate. References to the tag also appear inside `examples`, `resume-protocol`, and `rules` sections.
- `hooks/briefing/context.js` lines 22-63 already plumbs `role` into the context object. `memberContext()` / `leadContext()` (lines 57-63) call `render('member' | 'lead', ctx)`. Role plumbing is in place; only template sections need updating.
- `hooks/stop.js` lines 632-647 reads tags via `parseTurnTags(text)` and then unconditionally blocks turn-end if `!tags.kind`. The success path that follows (lines 698-720) depends on `tags.kind` for outbox-append and `manifest.lastKind` serialization. `decideStopBlock` at lines 433-471 takes `kind` via its call-site arg; the strict-mailbox-resolution gate inside is independent of the kind-tag requirement.
- `hooks/mailbox.js` lines 799-805 — `synthesizeSummary(body)` already derives a first-line summary fallback. Lead's `lastSummary` will benefit transparently once the missing-kind block stops short-circuiting the success path.
- `hooks/protocol/manifest.js` line 90 — null `lastKind` is already accepted. No schema change.
- `hooks/actors.js::formatMemberList` (line 1068) and `hooks/commands/status.js` (line 52) render null `lastKind` as `-` / `'(none yet)'` respectively. No "broken" indicator. The new default-to-`'progress'` behavior keeps `lastKind` populated for leads even on prose-only turns.
- Test runner: `tests/run.js` with plain Node assertions from `tests/lib/assert`. Goldens live under `tests/golden/`. Existing `tests/role-gate.test.js` already exercises lead Stop behavior with a tag.

### Technical Constraints
- A lead prose-only turn cannot pass through with `tags.kind = null` because outbox-append (`stop.js:700`) and manifest-update (`stop.js:706`, `:807`) serialize `tags.kind` into persistent state. Solution: synthesize `effectiveTurnKind(role, parsedKind)` after the role check, defaulting leads' missing `kind` to `'progress'`.
- The strict mailbox-resolution gate (unresolved consumed messages) is independent of the kind-tag requirement and must keep blocking leads with unresolved mail. Only the missing-kind block becomes member-only.
- The `<|report ack="..." reason="..."|>` and `<|report reply-to="..." ...|>` metadata tags must continue to work for leads without a `kind`, so leads can still acknowledge or reply to mailbox messages while emitting prose-only turns.
- SessionStart runs once per session. Existing live lead sessions on v1.7.3 keep their original briefing; only sessions spawned after the plugin cache refresh see the new briefing. This is the desired behavior — no retroactive change risk.
- The lead and member briefings have separate goldens (`tests/golden/briefing-lead.md`, `tests/golden/briefing-member.md`) verified by `tests/briefing-render.test.js`. Member golden MUST remain byte-identical.

## Approach

### Architecture
Single source of truth lives in **two places** working in lockstep:

1. **Briefing template** (`hooks/briefing/template.js`) — sections that mention or require the kind tag use `ctx.role === 'member'` gating via early-return, identical to the existing `listener-arm` pattern. Lead briefings omit the tag instructions, the tag examples, the "end with the kind tag" line in resume-protocol, and the kind-tag rule line in rules. They keep all other guidance (listener protocol, mailbox semantics, ack/reply-to metadata).

2. **Stop hook** (`hooks/stop.js`) — introduce `LEAD_DEFAULT_KIND = 'progress'` constant + small helper `effectiveTurnKind(role, parsedKind)` that returns `parsedKind` when present, else `'progress'` for leads, else `parsedKind` (null) for members. Gate the existing `if (!tags.kind)` block on `state.role === 'member'`. Substitute `turnKind` (the helper result) for `tags.kind` everywhere it feeds outbox-append, manifest-update, and `decideStopBlock`. Tailor lead-specific reason text in three locations: (a) empty-body-and-no-summary branch, (b) `buildUnresolvedConsumedReason` near line 269 — point at `<|report ...|>` metadata tag instead of the kind tag, (c) **listener-block reason near line 478** — replace any "kind tag" wording with role-neutral "turn-end metadata" so leads no longer see instructions to re-emit the very footer this change removes. Audit `stop.js` for any other strings that hard-code "kind tag" in a user-facing message.

No manifest schema change. No list-members display change. No new env vars. No new exports.

## Risk Areas

- **R1 — Hidden `tags.kind` consumer:** `tags.kind` is referenced in multiple places inside `stop.js::handleInput`. Every reference downstream of the missing-kind block must be replaced with `turnKind`; missing one will produce a null leaking into the outbox or manifest. Mitigation: comprehensive grep for `tags.kind` in `stop.js` during US-001, fixture coverage for lead-no-tag in US-002 that asserts both outbox envelope `kind` field AND manifest `lastKind` field equal `'progress'`.
- **R2 — Briefing section discovery:** The tag is referenced in `footer-tag` (primary), `examples`, `resume-protocol`, and `rules` sections. Missing one will leave a dangling instruction in the lead briefing. Mitigation: pre-merge grep of `template.js` for `kind tag`, `<|report`, `kind="`, and `footer tag` matches; gate every match's containing section.
- **R3 — Golden drift on member side:** The lead golden must change; the member golden must not. Mitigation: US-002 asserts `briefing-member.md` is byte-identical to its pre-change state (via the existing `tests/briefing-render.test.js` golden diff plus a CI-grade check).
- **R4 — Copilot's pre-applied edits as starting point:** Copilot research overflowed into implementation, leaving 14 modified files on `D:/ai-developer-toolkit` `main` (uncommitted). The diff matches this plan's design. **Operator decision needed** (logged in Open Questions): the impl member can either accept and Phase-5a-review those edits, or discard them and implement fresh from this plan. Discarding is safer (clean review trail); accepting is faster (saves ~30 minutes of edit work).
- **R5 — Strict-mailbox-resolution gate accidentally relaxed:** It's tempting to bundle "lead doesn't need kind tag" with "lead doesn't need to ack consumed messages." That would break crew coordination. The gate must stay independent. Mitigation: explicit fixture in US-002 that asserts lead-no-tag-with-unresolved-mail still blocks.
- **R6 — `resume-crew.js` side-effect contamination:** Copilot also fixed an unrelated PowerShell PID timing issue. If the impl member accepts Copilot's edits wholesale (per R4), they'll inherit this fix. **Mandatory pre-implementation step (regardless of Q1 outcome):** the impl member's very first action MUST be `git -C D:/ai-developer-toolkit restore -- plugins/crews/hooks/commands/resume-crew.js` to guarantee the v1.7.4 ship does not contain the unrelated change. Codified in the Implementation Strategy section.
- **R7 — `tests/version.test.js` brittleness:** The version test pins exact strings across multiple files. `bump-version.js 1.7.4` is the only safe way to update; manual edits will desync. Mitigation: US-003 mandates use of the script.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-1:** A lead turn ending with prose-only (no kind tag) passes the Stop hook cleanly (`decision: continue`, no `block`).
- **AC-2:** A member turn ending without a kind tag still BLOCKS at Stop with the existing error message (regression-guarded by a new fixture).
- **AC-3:** Lead's `manifest.lastSummary` gets populated from the prose first-line via `synthesizeSummary(tags.body)` when the tag is absent.
- **AC-4:** `list-members` view shows the lead's prose-derived summary in the Summary column without any "broken" indicator. `lastKind` displays as `progress` (the synthesized default).
- **AC-5:** A lead session **with an armed listener (manifest.listenerState='armed' + recent lastListenerSpawnAt)** and unresolved consumed mailbox messages still blocks at Stop with the lead-tailored "reply with `reply-to=` on a `<|report ...|>` metadata tag" reason. (Listener-armed precondition is mandatory in the fixture so the listener-reachability gate at `stop.js:478` does not preempt the unresolved-mail branch — see also AC-12.)
- **AC-6:** A lead emitting **prose plus** `<|report ack="<id>" reason="..."|>` (no `kind`) successfully resolves the acked message and passes Stop. (The empty-body block at `stop.js:692-730` still applies — leads cannot pass with a metadata-only turn that strips to an empty body via `parseTurnTags`. This is intentional: the empty-body guard remains role-neutral.)
- **AC-7:** Lead SessionStart briefing OMITS mandatory kind-tag instructions, the kind-tag-mandatory examples, the "end with kind tag" line in resume-protocol, and the kind-tag-required line in rules. Lead briefing **PRESERVES** ack/reply metadata tag syntax + at least one ack-tag and one reply-to-tag example so leads can still resolve consumed mail. Lead briefing **INCLUDES** a short explicit clause ("Leads do NOT need to append a routine `<|report kind=...|>` footer; metadata tags for ack/reply-to remain available when needed.") to avoid silent-omission ambiguity during the v1.7.3 → v1.7.4 transition. Member briefing remains byte-identical to v1.7.3.
- **AC-8:** Existing test suite passes. 5 new fixtures added per US-002 (F-A1 lead-prose-only-passes-with-progress-default, F-A2 member-no-tag-blocks-regression, F-A5 lead-armed-with-unresolved-mail-blocks, F-A6 lead-prose-plus-ack-resolves-without-kind, F-A12 lead-never-armed-blocks-with-role-neutral-wording).
- **AC-9:** `plugins/crews/CLAUDE.md` has a v1.7.4 section that explicitly documents the role-asymmetric behavior plus the rationale so future contributors don't "fix" the lead path back to symmetric.
- **AC-10:** Version stamps in all 5 manifest/marketplace files and `tests/version.test.js` agree on `1.7.4`. `node plugins/crews/scripts/bump-version.js 1.7.4` was the mechanism (not hand-edits).
- **AC-11:** Branch pushed to both `Evyatar108` and `gim-home` remotes. Merge to `main` proceeds per the v1.7.3 precedent (member-driven direct merge authorized **per the operator's 2026-05-28 spawn-prompt pre-authorization quoted verbatim: _"Multi-remote push (Evyatar108 + gim-home). Member-driven direct merge authorized per recent precedent."_** — this language is the audit-trail anchor; the impl member's commit and merge messages should reference it).
- **AC-12:** A lead session **without an armed listener** still blocks at Stop with the existing listener-reachability message — except the message is updated to use role-neutral "turn-end metadata" wording instead of "kind tag" for leads, so the user-facing string is consistent with the new role-asymmetric behavior. The block reason itself is unchanged (listener-reachability gate stays role-symmetric).

## Suggested Decomposition

US-001 and US-002 share files (`stop.js` + tests that exercise it; `template.js` + tests + goldens) and must serialize. US-003 is the version stamp + docs; it depends on US-001 + US-002 landing first so the version flip lines up with the behavioral + test changes. This is a serial-only decomposition — the file overlap and dependency chain leave no useful parallel work.

### Cluster: implementation-and-tests
- Stories: US-001, US-002
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`plugins/crews/hooks/stop.js`, `plugins/crews/hooks/briefing/template.js`]; exclusive=[]; risk=high. US-001 changes the code; US-002 changes the tests + goldens that verify it. Splitting them across parallel jobs would risk a transient state where the tests fail against unmodified code (or vice versa).
- `execution_mode` rationale: serialize because the test fixtures depend on the exact code changes in US-001. Running them as a single impl member keeps the diff coherent.

### Cluster: docs-and-version
- Stories: US-003
- Phase: 2
- Depends on: implementation-and-tests
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[]; exclusive=[`plugins/crews/CLAUDE.md`, `plugins/crews/CHANGELOG.md`, `plugins/crews/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `plugins/crews/.github/plugin/plugin.json`, `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, `.github/plugin/marketplace.json`, `plugins/crews/tests/version.test.js`]; risk=low.
